challenge.better_approach: Raise the budgets: that hides the redundant work and grows with every proof named, so no. Delete the teeth: then nothing at these addresses says the anchor rules hold together. Reading the seal is the smallest move that keeps the claim.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the named proofs are sealed green over their current closures when these two seal: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py names cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py, so it reads red until cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py reseals green, and a reseal that takes them in the other order reads red on a first pass. That is the correct red, not a flake; the builder seals cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py before cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py. Also that standing() reads the working copy's seals, so the tooth reads the tree it runs in, the same as component_color.
challenge.prior_art: validation_store.standing() already checks red, missing and fingerprint-moved seals; component_color reads the same seals.
challenge.real_collision: Law 8 (prove, then trust): reading a sibling's seal is trusting a proven peer, which is Law 8's whole return, provided the fingerprint is checked. With it, no collision.

answers.falsifier: Done when: both proofs, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py, seal green solo through bin/cairn test within their declared PROOF_TIMEOUT_S, once the standing proofs they name are sealed green over their current closures AND each standing-proof tooth (cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py::test_the_anchor_and_hollow_proofs_stay_green, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py::test_the_standing_hollow_proofs_stay_green) reads red when one named proof's seal is red, and reads red when a named proof's seal is green but its source_fingerprint no longer matches the proof's current closure; each case is planted in a scratch component (a proof file beside its seal file, the path validations_path_for derives) and asked through the same helper the tooth uses AND neither tooth runs a standing proof as a subprocess: an AST scan of both files finds no subprocess call naming a proof path, and each tooth's answer comes from cairn.tools.validation_store.validation_store.standing(path)['proven'] for every named proof. Wrong intent if a tooth needs a behaviour a seal cannot carry (a cross-proof interaction that only a fresh run shows).
answers.from_idea: none, because akienasus_cc_0 relayed it on 2026-11-21 with measurements over cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_anchor_ignores_instrument_commits.py and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_skips_only_the_instrument.py, and the orchestrator added the fingerprint constraint
answers.how: Replace each tooth's subprocess loop with a call to cairn.tools.validation_store.validation_store.standing over the same named proofs, asserting proven for each and putting standing()'s why in the assertion message. standing() already reds a missing seal, a red seal, and a green seal whose source_fingerprint no longer matches the closure it recorded (cairn/tools/validation_store/validation_store.py, standing), the same reading component_color makes, so the tooth trusts no stale green. Put the loop in one helper per file, e.g. _all_standing(paths), so a fixture tooth can ask it of planted paths. Add teeth for clause 2 (plant a scratch component with cairn.tools.scratch.scratch.scratch_dir: a proof file and its seal, once with verdict red, once green with a source_fingerprint that cannot match) and clause 3 (an AST scan over both files). PROVES keys this ticket's clauses to those teeth, and the existing keys (79aa8b19a840, 763379e32e3b) stay on the rewritten teeth. PROOF_TIMEOUT_S is lowered to what the remaining teeth measure, never raised.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (re-running a sealed proof re-derives a settled answer); Law 8 (prove, then trust: a proven peer's seal is leaned on, and a hollow green is worse than a red); Law 9 (a stale seal is not green); RULE 1 (the tester reads seals through validation_store's public interface, a tool with users).
answers.what: The tester's two standing-proof teeth ask whether the hollow proofs they name stand proven right now by reading their seals through cairn.tools.validation_store.validation_store.standing, fingerprint included, instead of re-running them, so both proofs seal green inside their own budgets and still read red over a red or stale seal.

bullets.text: Two tester teeth stop re-running proofs that carry their own seals and read standing() instead, fingerprint included; the slow red at tester's PROVED gate goes.
